Patch Notes

4.2.1

A security and assurance-integrity patch: remediation of the 14-finding external audit of v4.2.0. Every code-level finding is fixed with an adversarial regression test mirroring the audit's own reproduction.

What changed

  • Truthful self-assessment (LPOS-01, LPOS-02 — Critical/High). The compliance

module is now a control readiness monitor: it never emits "compliant" or "effective" about itself. Fresh installs report not_assessed / insufficient_evidence; distinct audit runs and days are counted honestly (21 controls in one execution is one run); statuses carry attestation: false, issued_by_cpa: false; structural checks are labeled as structural evidence and organizational criteria are listed as requiring human evidence.

  • Monitor hardening (LPOS-03, LPOS-04 — Critical/High). No shell execution

anywhere; executable checks come only from the admin-owned monitor/approved-checks.json — agent-registered services can no longer define commands or receive credentials. Tokens are bound to their connector's fixed origin, token files must live in the monitor secrets directory, private/loopback/metadata addresses are refused for agent-supplied URLs, and redirects are refused.

  • Verified approval identity (LPOS-05 — High). Approvals now require an assertion

minted by a registered channel verifier; a fabricated MessageIdentity with an allowlisted sender string is rejected. Live consequential adapters require a real provider-signature verifier and a verified round trip.

  • Dashboard boundary (LPOS-06, LPOS-09 — High/Medium). Session-token auth on every

API route, Host validation (kills DNS rebinding), Origin checks, JSON-only capped bodies, security headers, generic errors, mandatory loopback; the scanner no longer follows symlinks out of approved roots and out-of-root kanban paths are dropped.

  • State confidentiality (LPOS-07 — High). Databases and state files are created

0600 in 0700 directories regardless of umask, with startup permission repair.

  • Tamper-evident evidence (LPOS-08 — High). The event store and the compliance

history are hash-chained with verification (lpos doctor, python -m lpos_engine.compliance verify); the audit's row-removal and trigger-drop reproductions are now detected. Optional off-host checkpoint keys strengthen this.

  • Subprocess boundary (LPOS-10 — Medium). Streaming output caps (bounded peak

memory), process-group kill, allowlist environment, resource limits, executable pinning — documented honestly as privilege reduction, not a sandbox.

  • Release authenticity (LPOS-11 — Medium). Ed25519 release signing

(tools/sign_release.py, verified automatically by verify_release.py when present) and a CycloneDX SBOM (tools/make_sbom.py).

  • Always-on schema gate (LPOS-12 — Medium). A built-in structural meta-validator

runs in every install; a meta-invalid schema now fails installation instead of silently downgrading to JSON parsing.

  • Docs accuracy (LPOS-14 — Low) and SOC 2 program scaffolding (LPOS-13):

docs/SOC2-PROGRAM.md defines the organizational half a Type 2 examination needs.

What you will notice

Dashboard API calls now need the session token from dashboard/token. Monitor entries that carried their own commands now report unknown until an admin approves a check template. The compliance page is retitled "Control Readiness Report" and a fresh system honestly shows insufficient evidence instead of green.
